notes.b: Some events, such as a fire or a serious illness, cost far more than most households could pay at once. Insurance solves this by sharing the cost of those events across many people.
points: Insurance spreads the financial risk of an event, such as death, illness, fire or theft, across many people who each pay a premium. Only the few who suffer a loss are paid, out of the pool everyone has paid into.
The insured (the person covered, also called the policyholder) pays a premium to the insurer, and the insurer pays a stated sum when the insured event occurs.
Cover applies only to the events named in the policy, so an event the policy does not list is not paid for.
Insurance protects a household against a large, unexpected cost that it could not otherwise meet, for example illness, fire, theft or an accident.

Insurance pays the loss and not a profit, and the policyholder must give full and honest information when buying. Reading the policy and comparing quotes before buying helps you choose the right cover.
notes.tip: Higher Level answers should link insurance to managing risk in a family budget: a small regular premium is planned for so that a large unplanned cost does not wreck the budget.

notes.b: Exam questions ask you to explain the everyday words of insurance. Each one names a different person or part of the arrangement, so keep them apart.
points: Premium: the sum paid annually or in instalments to the insurance company to keep a policy in force. It is what you pay in.
Policy: the written document, a contract, setting out the terms and conditions of the cover, including what is covered and what is excluded.
Insurer: the insurance company that accepts the risk and pays claims.

Broker: an agent who advises the consumer on insurance and arranges cover with several insurance companies. A broker is paid by commission or a fee. This differs from an agent of one company, or buying direct from the insurer.
Claim: a request to the insurer for payment after a loss. Excess is the part of a claim that the policyholder pays. The sum assured (or sum insured) is the most the insurer will pay out.

The premium depends on the risk: age, health, claims history, location, the value of what is insured and security measures such as alarms all matter. The cover and excess you choose also change it, and a no-claims bonus lowers car premiums.
notes.tip: The premium is what you pay and the sum assured is what is paid out. The policy is the contract, not the payment, and a broker is not the insurer. Examiners ask you to explain premium and policy and to say what a broker does.

notes.b: PRSI is the State's own insurance scheme. It works like insurance because contributions made while working protect you against losing income later.
points: PRSI is the State's social insurance scheme. Workers (employees, employers and the self-employed) pay contributions, related to pay, into the Social Insurance Fund. Entitlement to its benefits depends on a record of contributions, not on means.
PRSI is a compulsory scheme set by law, not a private policy chosen by the individual. It is State-run and its benefits are not paid by an insurer, whereas private insurance is voluntary and private.

PRSI-linked payments include Jobseeker's Benefit, Illness Benefit, maternity benefit, Carer's Benefit and the contributory State pension. Others are the widow's or widower's pension and treatment benefit for dental and optical care.
It counts as insurance because contributions pay for protection against loss of income through unemployment, illness, retirement, bereavement or maternity.
Different PRSI classes carry different benefits, and low earners may be exempt from paying.
notes.tip: If asked to define PRSI, say it is compulsory and State-run, with contributions giving an entitlement to benefits. Do not call these benefits payments from an insurer.

notes.b: The public health system is available to everyone, but some people want more choice or quicker treatment. Private health insurance is a voluntary policy that pays towards those costs.
points: Private health insurance pays towards hospital, consultant and other medical costs, within the terms of the policy. It is voluntary and held alongside the public health system.
Advantages: choice of private or semi-private hospital accommodation, help with consultant fees, and shorter waiting times for some treatment.

Cover can include access to outpatient clinics, day-care, convalescence (recovery time) after treatment, some GP fees, some dental and optical cover, and treatment abroad. It also gives peace of mind.
Premiums may qualify for tax relief at source, which reduces the cost of cover.
When choosing a plan, compare the level of cover, premiums, excess, waiting periods, hospital choice and what is excluded. Compare insurers and plans.
Premiums are set by plan, not by your health (community rating), but joining late costs more.
Providers include Vhi (the largest), Laya, Irish Life Health and Level Health. The regulator is the Health Insurance Authority.
notes.tip: When asked for two advantages of private health insurance, pick from private or semi-private accommodation, consultant fees, shorter waits, convalescence, outpatient clinics or tax relief at source. If asked for a provider, name Vhi, Laya, Irish Life Health or Level Health.

notes.b: A household faces several different risks: damage to the home, loss of belongings, a car accident, trips abroad. Each has its own type of cover.
points: Buildings insurance covers the structure of the home (walls, roof, fixtures) against damage such as fire, storm, flood and subsidence. Mortgage lenders usually require it.

Contents insurance covers furniture, appliances, clothes, valuables and personal belongings against loss or damage such as theft and fire. An all-risks extension covers items outside the home, such as phones and bicycles.
Buildings and contents cover can be combined in one household policy, which may also include public liability and temporary accommodation.

Car insurance: third-party cover is required by law before a car is driven on public roads. It covers damage and injury to other people, not the policyholder's own car. Third party, fire and theft adds cover for those events, and comprehensive covers the most.

Travel insurance covers medical costs, cancelled trips and lost luggage abroad. Mobile phone insurance covers loss, theft or damage to a phone. Income protection, holiday, public liability and pet insurance are other types.
Insure for the correct value, because underinsurance means a reduced payout. Keep an inventory and receipts, state security measures, keep the policy up to date and report claims promptly.
notes.tip: Buildings insurance covers the structure and contents covers belongings, so a tenant needs contents, not buildings. For three types of insurance a consumer might need, name health, house (buildings or contents) and car, plus travel.

notes.b: Death is certain to happen, so this cover is called assurance rather than insurance. It pays a sum so that dependants are looked after if the insured person dies.
points: Life assurance pays a lump sum to the insured person's family or beneficiary (dependants) on death, either during the policy term or after it, depending on the type.
Term assurance covers a set period and pays only if death occurs within that period. There is no payout if the insured survives, and it is generally the cheapest type.
Whole-of-life assurance lasts for life, as long as premiums are paid, and pays an agreed sum on death whenever it occurs. It is dearer than term cover.
Endowment assurance pays a sum at the end of a set term or on earlier death, combining cover with saving.

A mortgage protection policy is term assurance taken out with a mortgage. Its sum assured falls with the mortgage balance, so if the insured dies before the mortgage is repaid, the debt is cleared. Lenders normally require it.

Convertible term assurance can be converted into a longer-term policy, such as whole-of-life, during the term without a new health check. Serious illness cover and income protection are related cover.
Benefits of life assurance: financial security for dependants after a premature death, help clearing a mortgage or debts, and peace of mind. Some policies can be cashed in or act as savings.
notes.tip: For one difference between term and whole-of-life, say term pays only if death occurs within the term while whole-of-life pays whenever death occurs. Do not say term cover pays back premiums. Mortgage protection is a common question.

keyTerms.definition: The sum paid annually or in instalments to the insurance company to keep a policy in force.
The written details of the terms and conditions of the insurance cover.
An agent who advises the consumer on insurance and arranges cover with insurers.
Life assurance that covers a set period and pays only if death occurs within it.
Life assurance that lasts for the insured person's lifetime, provided premiums are paid, and pays an agreed sum on death.
Life assurance that pays a sum at the end of a set term or on earlier death, combining cover with saving.
Term assurance taken out with a mortgage, which clears the outstanding debt if the insured dies during the mortgage term.
Voluntary cover that pays for private hospital and consultant costs within the policy terms.
Cover for the structure of a home against damage such as fire, storm and flood.

questions.prompt: Explain the term premium, and describe one difference between term assurance and whole-of-life assurance.
questions.model: Premium: the sum paid annually or in instalments to the insurance company to keep the policy in force. Difference: term assurance covers a set period and pays only if death occurs within that period; whole-of-life assurance lasts for life, as long as premiums are paid, and pays an agreed sum on death.

questions.prompt: Discuss why a family should consider buying household insurance and health insurance, and explain the role of a broker in choosing cover. Refer to the difference between a policy and a premium.
questions.model: Household insurance: buildings cover protects the structure of the home, usually required by mortgage lenders; contents cover protects furniture and belongings; car insurance is required by law. Health insurance: private cover for hospital and consultant costs, with choice of accommodation and shorter waiting times. Insurance protects against a large unexpected cost. Premium: the sum paid to keep cover in force. Policy: the written terms and conditions, which set out what is covered. Broker: an agent who advises on the cover needed and arranges it with insurers, comparing terms for the family.
